purpose: Test whether the standardized local photon environment measured within Thalassia canopies predicts short-term reserve change, without reopening the failed bulk Secchi x depth proxy or the bounded qualitative epiphyte field.

relationship_to_existing_tampa_results.bulk_light_result: The frozen Secchi-derived benthic-light proxy did not support blade-length or shoot-density trajectories.
relationship_to_existing_tampa_results.epiphyte_result: Qualitative annual EpiphyteDensity did not support the simple prediction that higher burden is a year-ahead stress signal; the primary within-node coefficient was positive and the 2016 sensitivity overlapped zero.
relationship_to_existing_tampa_results.new_question: Does direct high-frequency photon exposure at a frozen standardized position inside the living canopy, measured over the same biological interval as TNC change, explain reserve depletion that coarse bay-segment light and qualitative epiphyte categories missed?
relationship_to_existing_tampa_results.hard_boundary: Do not reclassify EpiphyteDensity categories, epiphyte types, lags or annual windows. The new test must use direct optical measurements.

sampling_frame.cohort: Contemporaneously baseline-Thalassia-positive stable fixed-transect nodes, census-oriented where feasible.
sampling_frame.below_precision_gate: Below 30 analyzable nodes or below 8 nodes in any core bay, retain effect estimates and uncertainty as a pilot and do not use a null to reject optical stress.

sensor_meter_mark_selection.rule: Select the optical deployment meter mark before any PAR data are inspected and without using mapped edge distance, water clarity or preliminary light.
sensor_meter_mark_selection.primary_thalassia_rule: Among contemporaneously Thalassia-positive meter marks, choose the mark closest to the median site_m of all contemporaneously vegetated meter marks in that node; exact tie -> lower site_m.
sensor_meter_mark_selection.provenance: Same edge-independent representative-placement principle already frozen for the direct hydrodynamic programme.
sensor_meter_mark_selection.prohibited_rescue: Do not move the PAR logger to a brighter/darker or more accessible meter mark after preliminary optical inspection. If the chosen mark cannot satisfy the frozen sensor geometry, the node is optical-primary-ineligible.

deployment.preferred_calendar: Co-deploy with the frozen July 24 through September 3 event-stress campaign so PAR and pre/post TNC are measured over the same biological interval.
deployment.primary_exposure_window: Use the common calendar overlap shared by confirmatory nodes after frozen PAR QC; do not extend or shift the window after TNC inspection.

within_canopy_sensor.measurement: One frozen underwater photosynthetically active photon measurement quantity with a single angular-response class across all outcome-bearing channels; either 2π cosine-corrected PPFD or 4π scalar photon fluence-rate, never a mixture within the primary study.
within_canopy_sensor.placement: One fixed response-independent within-canopy sampling position per node, targeted at 50% of baseline canopy height above the bed.
within_canopy_sensor.geometry_rule: Exact sensor model, angular orientation, proportional canopy-height placement, allowable height tolerance, mounting hardware and shading-clearance rule must be frozen in a response-independent physical pilot before outcome-bearing deployment.
within_canopy_sensor.eligibility_boundary: If the frozen sensor position cannot remain submerged and physically within the canopy under field conditions, the node is not confirmatory for the optical primary rather than moving the sensor after inspection.

vertical_representativeness_pilot.purpose: Verify that one frozen proportional canopy height is a defensible proxy for the local within-canopy light environment before outcome-bearing deployment.
vertical_representativeness_pilot.design: At a response-independent physical-pilot subset spanning shallow/tall canopies, obtain short simultaneous or rapidly repeated PAR profiles at 25%, 50% and 75% of canopy height plus one above-canopy reference.
vertical_representativeness_pilot.decision_rule: Freeze one proportional within-canopy height before the first outcome-bearing TNC sample. The pilot may change the default 50% rule only before TNC response exists and only using optical representativeness/field geometry, never biological outcome.
vertical_representativeness_pilot.no_rescue: After outcome-bearing deployment begins, do not change sensor height by node or select the vertical level with the strongest TNC association.
vertical_representativeness_pilot.acceptance_summary: Minimum 12 pilot nodes / >=3 per bay; simultaneous 25%, 50%, 75% canopy-height PAR plus above-canopy reference; selected single height must have median absolute relative DLI error <=15%, >=80% node-days within +/-25%, and bay-specific median relative bias <=20%.

angular_response_semantics.freeze_timing: Choose exactly one class before the response-independent optical method pilot is interpreted and before outcome-bearing deployment.
angular_response_semantics.same_class_rule: Every outcome-bearing within-canopy sensor/channel and every paired above-canopy reference used for canopy transmittance must use the same frozen angular-response class.
angular_response_semantics.matched_reference_rule: In-water calibration reference must use the same angular-response class as the primary outcome sensors. Cross-class cosine↔scalar calibration is not accepted in v1.

reporting.2pi_cosine_ppfd: Report the primary exposure as daily light integral of hemispherical cosine-corrected photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD).
reporting.4pi_scalar_ppffr: Report the primary exposure as daily integral of scalar photosynthetic photon flux fluence rate (PPFFR/scalar photon irradiance); do not relabel it as cosine-corrected PPFD.

angular_response_semantics.rationale: Cosine and scalar quantum sensors integrate different angular light fields. A canopy changes angular light distribution, so agreement under one calibration geometry does not make the two quantities interchangeable in situ.
angular_response_semantics.future_transfer_boundary: A future study may validate cross-class angular transfer under representative underwater directional light fields, but no such transfer is authorized for this v1 primary.

deployment.coverage_rule: Each confirmatory node must retain >=85% valid PAR observations across the common overlap after only predeclared QC.
deployment.fouling_rule: Sensor anti-fouling method, cleaning schedule if any, optical-reference checks, fouling/drift exclusion rule, burial/exposure rule and interpolation/gap rule must be frozen before deployment.

daily_dli_qc.valid_day_rule: A daily DLI is valid only when >=90% of scheduled astronomical-daylight observations are present and no continuous daylight gap exceeds 30 minutes.
daily_dli_qc.node_rule: Primary node mean DLI uses only valid days and requires at least 30 valid daily DLIs within the frozen common overlap, in addition to the >=85% overall PAR coverage rule.
daily_dli_qc.interpolation_boundary: Linear interpolation is allowed only for daylight gaps <=30 minutes. Longer daylight gaps invalidate that node-day; do not reconstruct them from neighboring nodes or above-canopy references.
daily_dli_qc.rationale: DLI integration is sensitive to missing observations during daylight; overall row coverage alone is insufficient.
daily_dli_qc.daylight_definition: Astronomical local sunrise-to-sunset for each node/date; nighttime is integrated as zero but does not count toward daylight-coverage eligibility.

calendar_interpretation_boundary.selection_provenance: July 24-September 3 was selected response-independently for the hot-fresh event-stress programme, not optimized for optical contrast.
calendar_interpretation_boundary.reason_for_sharing: Co-deployment places optical and hot-fresh forcing on the same biological interval and reuses the same pre/post TNC samples.
calendar_interpretation_boundary.null_interpretation: An optical null weakens direct within-canopy DLI as a reserve driver over this fixed late-summer interval only; it is not evidence that light is unimportant in other seasons.
calendar_interpretation_boundary.no_rescue: Do not shift the optical window to another season after seeing TNC. A different seasonal optical hypothesis requires a separately frozen future study.

primary_exposure.name: mean_daily_within_canopy_dli
primary_exposure.definition: For each valid day, integrate calibrated within-canopy PAR over 24 h to daily light integral; primary node exposure is the arithmetic mean DLI across valid days in the frozen common overlap.
primary_exposure.direction: higher mean daily within-canopy DLI predicts higher post-exposure TNC after accounting for pre-exposure TNC
primary_exposure.no_threshold_search: No low-light threshold is used in the primary model. Do not introduce a percent-surface-light or DLI cutoff after observing TNC.

minimum_variation_gate.rule: At least two bays must each contain >=6 analyzable nodes and >=3 distinct node-level DLI values. Otherwise the optical primary is non-estimable rather than dropping water_body or selecting a favorable subset.

primary_exposure.angular_semantics: The column name mean_daily_within_canopy_dli is a computational placeholder. Scientific reporting must name the frozen angular-response quantity (2π cosine PPFD DLI or 4π scalar photon-fluence integral) recorded in the method freeze.
primary_exposure.biological_quantity_boundary: The sensor measures the local underwater photon field at one standardized canopy position. It is not a direct measure of photons absorbed by moving Thalassia leaf area, whole-canopy photosynthesis, or leaf-integrated dose.

reserve_response.pre_tnc: Use the same pre-exposure TNC samples and frozen HPLC/tissue protocol as the event-stress/clonal programme.
reserve_response.post_tnc: Use the same post-exposure TNC samples and frozen HPLC/tissue protocol as the event-stress/clonal programme.
reserve_response.temporal_pairing: Confirmatory pre/post TNC interval remains 39-45 days under the already frozen destructive-sampling guardrail.
reserve_response.inferential_unit: stable transect node; PAR rows and TNC cores are repeated measurements, not ecological replicates
reserve_response.shared_core_rule: Use the same two pre/post TNC rounds already frozen for the event-stress/clonal programme. Optical sampling does not authorize an additional destructive TNC round.

primary_analysis.uncertainty: 10,000-replicate water-body-stratified stable-node bootstrap; seed 20261005; two-sided percentile 95% interval for standalone status; same resamples yield 97.5% interval for the predeclared two-test forcing family.

support_rule.boundary: Do not switch to a one-sided test, a low-light threshold, or a different PAR aggregation after inspection.

primary_analysis.missing_data_rule: complete-case confirmatory analysis under predeclared PAR/TNC QC; do not impute DLI or TNC to rescue sample size

canopy_structure.role: Describe whether low within-canopy DLI reflects canopy structure/self-shading; cannot replace a null primary DLI result.

epiphyte_biomass.measurement: standardized epiphyte dry mass or ash-free dry mass per leaf area from a frozen leaf-age/position class
epiphyte_biomass.role: Secondary explanation for leaf-surface optical load. Qualitative historical EpiphyteDensity is not reused as the primary mechanism variable.

paired_leaf_optics.status: response-independent laboratory pilot required before inferential use
paired_leaf_optics.idea: On a standardized sampled leaf segment, quantify PAR/spectral transmittance intact and after one validated gentle epiphyte-removal method; derive paired epiphyte-associated transmittance loss.
paired_leaf_optics.pilot_boundary: The cleaning/removal method must be shown not to materially alter cleaned-leaf optical properties in a response-independent Thalassia pilot before using this metric.
paired_leaf_optics.role: Physical attribution diagnostic for epiphyte shading only; not required for the broader actual-light primary.

turbidity_context.measurement: optional co-located turbidity or suspended-particle proxy
turbidity_context.role: Response-independent context only; do not add/remove it from the primary DLI model after TNC inspection.

paired_above_canopy_reference.purpose: Distinguish low actual within-canopy light caused by local canopy/leaf attenuation from low incident/above-canopy underwater irradiance caused by cloud, water-column attenuation or bay-scale optical forcing.
paired_above_canopy_reference.cohort: Nested response-independent optical-attribution subset. Nodes remain eligible for the primary within-canopy DLI -> TNC test even if no paired reference sensor is available.
paired_above_canopy_reference.measurement: Simultaneous PAR above the local canopy at the same node, using the same sensor family/calibration/QC and a frozen clearance above canopy.

geometry.requirement: Reference sensor must remain submerged and outside the standing leaf canopy while avoiding mount shadow. Exact clearance tolerance frozen in the response-independent optical pilot.

metrics.above_canopy_mean_daily_dli: Mean valid daily DLI measured simultaneously above the local canopy over the same common interval.

paired_above_canopy_reference.physical_gate: Report paired node-level transmittance/attenuation distribution and two-sided node-bootstrap interval for mean canopy_optical_attenuation. This is a physical attribution diagnostic, not a second biological primary.

interpretation.primary_supported_attenuation_positive: Consistent with biologically consequential low actual light plus a local canopy-associated optical gradient.
interpretation.primary_supported_attenuation_weak: Actual light predicts reserve state, but the cause may be incident/water-column forcing rather than canopy/epiphyte attenuation.
interpretation.primary_unsupported_attenuation_positive: Canopy changes local light, but this measured attenuation is not shown to deplete reserve over the frozen interval.

paired_above_canopy_reference.no_rescue: Do not replace a null primary within-canopy DLI result with attenuation, transmittance or above-canopy DLI as a new primary after inspection.

competing_epiphyte_interpretations.optical_stress_prediction: Higher measured epiphyte biomass and/or paired epiphyte-associated transmittance loss should correspond to lower actual within-canopy light and, if biologically consequential over the interval, lower post-TNC after pre-TNC.
competing_epiphyte_interpretations.mature_canopy_marker_prediction: Historical qualitative epiphyte burden may covary with leaf age, canopy persistence or favorable microsite state without independently reducing actual light enough to explain reserve depletion.
competing_epiphyte_interpretations.decision_boundary: Do not infer epiphyte stress from taxonomy/category alone. The optical mechanism follows direct light and physical optical measurements.

relationship_to_event_stress.shared_interval: PAR may be co-deployed with temperature/salinity and share pre/post TNC, but hot-fresh and optical models remain separately frozen.
relationship_to_event_stress.cross_exposure_diagnostic: Before TNC results are inspected, report the node-level correlation between mean_daily_within_canopy_dli and joint_hot_fresh_hours_30_25 if both are estimable.
relationship_to_event_stress.interpretation_boundary: If both optical and hot-fresh primaries support, do not claim statistically independent effects without a separately powered joint model frozen before TNC response access.
relationship_to_event_stress.no_rescue_rule: A null/non-estimable hot-fresh result cannot be rescued by adding PAR, and a null optical result cannot be rescued by adding temperature/salinity covariates post hoc.

relationship_to_future_meadow_state.primary_role: The immediate optical mechanism endpoint is reserve change, not binary loss or annual reappearance.
relationship_to_future_meadow_state.boundary: Secondary only; cannot rescue a null light-to-TNC primary. Binary re-recording remains prohibited as recovery.

site_template_boundary.statement: A cross-node DLI association can still reflect persistent local site properties, but the pre/post TNC response and synchronized common exposure interval provide a dynamic process test that is less compatible with a purely static site-template explanation.
site_template_boundary.limitation: Time-varying common causes such as turbidity events, nutrients, hypoxia or disturbance may still covary with light and TNC.
site_template_boundary.claim_rule: Supported within-canopy photon exposure -> TNC is described as a prospective local optical-environment/reserve association; causal optical stress and whole-leaf absorbed dose are not claimed without stronger measurement/manipulation.

pre_outcome_freeze_required: final contemporaneous node list and alternates
within-canopy proportional-height placement rule and tolerance
pre/post TNC temporal and destructive-sampling rules
any paired intact-versus-cleaned leaf optical method and response-independent damage pilot
response-independent vertical PAR profile pilot and final proportional-height rule
daily DLI valid-day coverage and maximum daytime-gap rule
paired above-canopy reference subset and clearance geometry
in-water cross-calibration of every outcome-bearing PAR sensor/channel
fixed 90% daylight coverage / 30-minute maximum daylight gap DLI rule
frozen cleaning/antifouling interval from optical pilot
single primary optical angular-response class (2pi_cosine_ppfd or 4pi_scalar_ppffr) and matched-class calibration reference
claim_boundary: This study tests direct canopy-scale light exposure, not the failed bay-segment Secchi proxy.
Do not translate a supported DLI coefficient into proof that epiphytes caused the low light unless the separate physical epiphyte-optics diagnostic supports that link.
Do not reuse historical qualitative EpiphyteDensity as the primary optical predictor.
Repeated PAR observations improve exposure measurement but do not substitute for node replication.
If fewer than 30 analyzable nodes remain or any core bay has fewer than 8, a null is a pilot null.
Do not use binary re-recording as a recovery endpoint.
The optical deployment meter mark is selected without using preliminary PAR or mapped edge distance; sensor placement cannot be moved to manufacture exposure contrast.

Within-canopy DLI is the biological exposure primary. Canopy/epiphyte optical attribution requires the separate paired above-canopy and/or leaf-optics diagnostics; low within-canopy DLI alone does not identify its optical source.
Daily-light-integral QC must protect the daylight integral itself; a node cannot remain primary-eligible solely because total row coverage exceeds 85% if daylight gaps make DLI unreliable.
Optical deployment reuses the already planned pre/post TNC rounds and does not justify additional destructive reserve sampling.

The July 24-September 3 calendar was chosen for event-stress climatology, not to maximize optical contrast; optical inference is explicitly interval-specific and cannot be generalized to all seasons from this deployment alone.

Optical confirmatory readiness additionally requires the response-independent sensor calibration, vertical representativeness, placement-repeatability, fouling-maintenance and DLI missingness gates in results/optical_pilot_acceptance_v1_contract.json.

Cosine-corrected PPFD and 4pi scalar photon fluence rate are distinct optical quantities and are not interchangeable in this primary. All outcome-bearing within/above-canopy channels and the calibration reference must use one matched frozen angular-response class.

A fixed underwater quantum sensor measures the local photon environment, not whole-leaf or whole-canopy absorbed photon dose. Leaf angle, motion, absorptance and vertical leaf-area distribution remain outside the primary exposure definition.
